primary_outcome_name: Voluntary activation (Central Activation Ratio, CAR) and quadriceps strength (Normalized Peak Torque, NPT, during MVIC) — two co-primary outcomes
primary_outcome_instrument_scale: CAR (%, 0-100 scale), CAR = [MVIC torque / (MVIC + superimposed-burst torque)] x 100, assessed via isokinetic dynamometer (Biodex System 3) with superimposed-burst technique; co-primary NPT in Nm/kg during MVIC
primary_timepoint: Post-intervention, i.e. after completion of the 10th a-tDCS session (baseline was assessed at 10 weeks post-ACLR, immediately before the first a-tDCS/sham session)
contrast_reported_primary: active a-tDCS + RPT vs sham a-tDCS + RPT
population_detail: Male nonprofessional athletes (volleyball, basketball, football), aged 18-40 years, in subacute recovery (~10 weeks post-surgery) following anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR); mean age 27.50 +/- 7.24 years, BMI 25.83 +/- 3.49 kg/m2; n=20 total (10 active, 10 sham); recruited at a single outpatient rehabilitation center in Isfahan, Iran.

published_estimate.quote: The active a-tDCS group demonstrated a significant improvement in CAR compared to the sham group (mean difference: 6.85%; 95% CI: 1.92–11.77; p = 0.01), while the sham group showed a slight, non-significant decrease (2.54%; p = 0/80). [sic, printed thus in the PLOS ONE PDF]  -- Abstract, Results paragraph (p. 1-2/21); this figure equals the post-intervention between-group difference in CAR means (99.34% active vs 92.49% sham; see Discussion, Section 3, p. 16/21, and Fig 5).

B_covariate_list: None used as covariates in the primary between-group model. Age and BMI were tested only for baseline between-group balance (Table 1, both P>0.05: age P=0.57, BMI P=0.88) and were not entered as covariates/adjustment terms in the CAR analysis.

registry_check.issues: 1) The paper declares TWO co-primary outcomes (Statistical analyses, p.10/21: 'The pre-specified primary outcomes were voluntary activation and quadriceps strength, measured as normalized peak torque during MVIC'), not CAR alone. Our registry line (outcome_var=CAR_post_all/CAR_pre_all) captures only one of the two co-primary outcomes; NPT/MVIC (the other co-primary outcome) is not represented. 2) covars_published=age,BMI in our registry does NOT match the paper: age and BMI were tested only for baseline group balance (Table 1, both P>0.05) and were NOT used as covariates/adjustment in the primary CAR model, which was a simple unadjusted independent t-test/Mann-Whitney U between-group comparison (B_covariates=none). 3) control_arm_matches could not be verified from the paper text alone: the manuscript never states the numeric coding of a 'group' variable (e.g., whether control/sham = 1 or 2) in the underlying dataset; this must be checked against the Zenodo dataset codebook (10.5281/zenodo.19831812), not the paper. The paper does clearly identify sham a-tDCS + RPT as the comparator/control arm and active a-tDCS + RPT as the intervention arm. 4) Internal inconsistency in the paper itself: the headline 'mean difference: 6.85%' in the Abstract is the POST-INTERVENTION (endpoint) between-group difference in CAR (99.34% active vs 92.49% sham), whereas the Results body text separately reports RELATIVE percent within-group changes for CAR as '+4.98%' (active, i.e. (99.34-94.62)/94.62*100) and '-2.54%' (sham, i.e. (92.49-94.90)/94.90*100) -- these are different quantities from the 6.85-point endpoint mean difference and could be confused with it. 5) The sham group's within-group CAR p-value is reported inconsistently across the paper: p=0.76 (Results, 'Voluntary activation' paragraph, compared to active group), p=0.59 (same paragraph, few lines later, as the paired within-group test), and 'p = 0/80' (Abstract; apparently a typographical rendering of 0.80 in the original PLOS PDF). 6) A separate non-parametric sensitivity analysis on CAR change scores (Delta = post-pre) using Mann-Whitney U is also reported (U=9.00, P=0.001; Results, p.12/21), distinct from and more significant than the primary endpoint-based estimate (MD=6.85%, CI 1.92-11.77, p=0.01) used for published_estimate above.

analysis_method_quote: All statistical analyses were conducted using SPSS software (version 18; IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA). The Shapiro-Wilk test was applied to assess the normality of data distribution prior to selecting appropriate statistical tests. Between-group comparisons (active a-tDCS vs. sham a-tDCS) were performed using independent t-tests for normally distributed variables and the Mann-Whitney U test for non-normally distributed data. Within-group comparisons (pre- vs. post-intervention) were analyzed using paired-sample t-tests or Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, depending on the distribution of the data. Effect sizes were calculated using Cohen's d, along with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), to determine the magnitude of observed changes. [...] No missing data were observed during the study; therefore, no imputation was performed, and all analyses were conducted using complete cases. All 20 participants who completed the intervention protocol were analyzed according to their assigned group (active or sham a-tDCS), consistent with a per-protocol approach. The pre-specified primary outcomes were voluntary activation and quadriceps strength, measured as normalized peak torque during MVIC. Secondary outcomes included functional, pain, and psychological scores, specifically KOOS, IKDC, VAS, and ACL-RSI. -- Materials and methods, 'Statistical analyses' section, p. 10/21.
notes: Field coded as 'neuromodulation' rather than 'physiotherapy_rehabilitation': the randomised, blinded contrast is active vs sham a-tDCS, while routine physical therapy (RPT) is held constant/identical across both arms; the trial is fundamentally testing a neuromodulation adjunct, embedded in a rehabilitation care pathway. intervention_delivered_by coded 'physiotherapist' because RPT and a-tDCS-session preparation were delivered by a trained physiotherapist (also a study investigator); note however that a-tDCS device settings (active vs sham) were configured by a separate independent, blinded, trained technician, and laboratory outcome measurements (MVIC/CAR) were performed by a separate blinded researcher -- the paper does not offer a single-role option that captures all of this. journal_requires_data_sharing coded 'yes' based on PLOS ONE's well-established mandatory data-availability policy (reflected here by the presence of a formal Data Availability Statement in every PLOS article, including this one), not from an explicit statement inside this specific paper. The trial registration number is given in the Abstract (IRCT20231113060048N1, registered 28 Dec 2023) and a full study protocol is listed as Supporting Information (S1 File, 'S1 Protocol', DOCX), supporting C_protocol_available='yes'. The original protocol reportedly specified quadriceps strength assessment at week 8 post-ACLR (moved to week 10) and hamstring-autograft-only inclusion (later broadened to allograft+autograft) -- both explicitly flagged by the authors as protocol deviations, which is relevant context for judging estimand/analysis-population changes versus the registration but does not by itself change the primary-outcome definition. No separate table with post-intervention SD for CAR was found in the paper (only means, extracted from Discussion text p.16/21 and Fig 5); hence followup_sd=null for both arms.
